rendered: The premise is reversed. The 10%[1] Mn sample, not the 50%[2] Mn sample, delivered more capacity: 212 mAh g^− 1[3] versus 164 mAh g^− 1[4], because Mn4+ ions are electrochemically inactive. So the 50%[5] Mn sample released less heat, not more. In the thermal decomposition tests the 10%[6] Mn sample released 901.4 J g^−1[7] and the 50%[8] Mn sample released 485.7 J g^−1[9]. The difference is 415.7[10] J/g of additional heat from the lower-Mn sample, not from the 50%[11] sample.
